concepts.title: The Four-Yoga Architecture
concepts.excerpt: Picture a house with one room at the center and four doors into it. One door is for people who can't sit still — they need to do.

concepts.title: Each Soul Is Potentially Divine
concepts.excerpt: A lioness, hunting, leaps at a flock of sheep and dies in the effort. Her cub is born motherless and the sheep raise it.

concepts.title: Religion Is Realisation, Not Belief
concepts.excerpt: You can study a map of France for a lifetime. Memorize every road, every river, the exact shape of the coast.

concepts.title: Strength Is the One Thing Needful
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda reduces the entire moral and spiritual life to one diagnostic and one cure.

concepts.title: Karma as Character-Formation
concepts.excerpt: Strike a piece of flint once and you get a spark. Strike it ten thousand times and you've started fires, cooked food, lit a life.

concepts.title: Work Without Attachment to Fruits
concepts.excerpt: A lotus leaf sits on the surface of a pond. Water washes over it all day.

concepts.title: Knowledge Is Uncovering, Not Acquiring
concepts.excerpt: An apple falls. Newton watches and "discovers" gravitation. But where was gravitation hiding before that — sitting in the apple?

concepts.title: Each Is Great in His Own Place
concepts.excerpt: You don't walk up to an apple tree and call it a failed oak. "To judge the apple tree you must take the apple standard, and for the oak, its own standard."

concepts.title: The Subjective Definition of Duty
concepts.excerpt: Try to define "duty" objectively and it dissolves in your hands. A Christian must eat beef to save a life; a Hindu must refuse it.

concepts.title: Pravṛtti and Nivṛtti
concepts.excerpt: Watch which way your whole life leans. One direction grabs: it pulls everything toward a center called "me" — more money, more name, more power, more mine.

concepts.title: We Help Ourselves, Not the World
concepts.excerpt: As a boy Vivekananda kept white mice in a box fitted with little wheels.

concepts.title: Ritual as Concretized Philosophy
concepts.excerpt: The cross didn't start as a Christian symbol. It was scratched into walls "among the Aztecs and the Phoenicians… before Christianity was, before Moses was born, before the Vedas were given out."

concepts.title: The Vyādha Gītā: End and Means Joined
concepts.excerpt: A proud young monk has spent years in the forest meditating, and he's got powers — a glance from him burns a quarrelsome bird to ashes.

concepts.title: Karma as Causation and Freedom
concepts.excerpt: Watch a fast river hit a hollow in the bank. The water spins into a whirlpool, churns there a while, then slips back out into the open current and flows on.

concepts.title: Bhakti as Supreme Love of God
concepts.excerpt: Most paths are means to an end — you do the work to get somewhere.

concepts.title: The Triangle of Love
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda draws love as a triangle — and the three corners are a test.

concepts.title: The Philosophy of Ishvara
concepts.excerpt: Take a lump of clay and make things from it — a mouse, an elephant, a pot.

concepts.title: The Need of Guru: Soul-to-Soul Transmission
concepts.excerpt: You can read spiritual books your whole life and stay spiritually dead.

concepts.title: Qualifications of Teacher and Taught
concepts.excerpt: Some men walk into a mango orchard and get to work — counting the leaves, measuring the twigs, comparing the colors of the branches, writing it all down, then arguing learnedly about their findings.

concepts.title: The Avatāra/Incarnation Doctrine
concepts.excerpt: When a huge tidal wave rolls in, every little brook and ditch fills to the brim — not by working, not by effort, just by the wave passing over.

concepts.title: Om, Sphoṭa, Word and Wisdom
concepts.excerpt: Open your mouth and make every sound it's capable of. Start at the very back of the throat — that's "A," the rawest, least-shaped sound there is.

concepts.title: Pratīka and Pratimā: Image-Worship
concepts.excerpt: A window does two jobs depending on how you use it. Look through it and you see the landscape beyond; the glass disappears, doing its work.

concepts.title: Iṣṭa-Niṣṭhā: The Chosen Ideal
concepts.excerpt: A man wants water, so he digs — three feet here, hits rock, moves on; three feet there, gives up; ten holes across the field, none deeper than his knee, and he dies of thirst on land soaked with water just below.

concepts.title: The Method and Means of Bhakti
concepts.excerpt: Here is Vivekananda at his most bracing about what actually counts. "The man who will mercilessly cheat widows and orphans and do the vilest deeds for money is worse than any brute even if he lives entirely on grass.

concepts.title: Rāja Yoga as the Science of Religion
concepts.excerpt: A chemist doesn't pray for the reaction to work — he goes to the lab, mixes the substances, watches what happens, and knows.

concepts.title: The Eight Limbs (Aṣṭāṅga)
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda lays out Patañjali's yoga as an eight-step staircase, and the steps are not arbitrary — each rests on the one below, and you cannot stand on a higher step until the lower one holds your weight.

concepts.title: Prāṇa and Ākāśa Cosmology
concepts.excerpt: Reduce everything — stars, bodies, thoughts, gravity, electricity, the chair, the sun — to its two ultimate ingredients, and Vivekananda says you get just two: a stuff and a force.

concepts.title: Prāṇāyāma Is Not Breathing
concepts.excerpt: A minister is imprisoned at the top of a high tower, left to die. His wife comes at night, and he tells her to bring a beetle, a drop of honey, a silken thread, some pack-thread, stout twine, and a rope.

concepts.title: Ojas: The Sublimation of Sexual Energy
concepts.excerpt: The energy that drives sexual desire and the energy that drives spiritual genius are, Vivekananda says, the same energy — just burned in different furnaces.

concepts.title: Kuṇḍalinī, Iḍā, Piṅgalā, Suṣumnā (1896)
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda describes a coiled energy sleeping at the base of the spine that, when roused, climbs a central channel and opens the mind layer by layer until the soul stands free.

concepts.title: The Superconscious (Samādhi)
concepts.excerpt: There are two ways to lose the sense of "I" — and they look similar from outside but are worlds apart.

concepts.title: Pratyāhāra: Control of the Mind
concepts.excerpt: Picture the most restless creature you can: a monkey. Now make it drunk — give it wine, so it's wilder.

concepts.title: Dhāraṇā, Dhyāna, Samādhi = Saṃyama
concepts.excerpt: Concentration deepens in three stages, and Vivekananda describes them as one continuous motion getting deeper.

concepts.title: The Sāṅkhya Psychology of Perception
concepts.excerpt: You're reading a book in your library. The clock on the wall strikes the hour.

concepts.title: Haṭha Yoga Produces Only Health
concepts.excerpt: A banyan tree can live five thousand years. Vivekananda points at it and shrugs.

concepts.title: The Necessity of Religion: The Struggle to Transcend the Senses
concepts.excerpt: Two camps were arguing about where religion started. One said it began with ancestor-worship — people couldn't believe their dead relatives were really gone, so they fed them, prayed to them, kept them around.

concepts.title: The Real Nature of Man: The Lion Among the Sheep
concepts.excerpt: A pregnant lioness leaps at a flock of sheep, and the leap kills her. A cub is born, motherless, and the sheep raise it.

concepts.title: Māyā Is a Statement of Fact, Not Illusion
concepts.excerpt: You've heard "the world is Māyā" and you filled in the meaning: the world is an illusion, a dream, not really there.

concepts.title: The Gods Grow as the Worshippers Grow
concepts.excerpt: Read the old scriptures and the gods look terrible. Indra drinks so much he falls down and babbles.

concepts.title: The Absolute and Manifestation: The Glass of Time, Space, and Causation
concepts.excerpt: Here's the question that won't go away, the one Vivekananda says "will always remain": how did the Infinite, the Absolute, become the finite — become this, the world of tables and stars and you?

concepts.title: Deification of the World: God in Everything
concepts.excerpt: The seller is doing math. What will it fetch? How fast are the bids rising?

concepts.title: Realisation vs Talk: The Boy Who Went to Death
concepts.excerpt: A rich man is performing a sacrifice that's supposed to require giving away everything he owns.

concepts.title: The Freedom of the Soul: Causeless Therefore Free
concepts.excerpt: A man lives in a forest, repeating day and night: Shivoham — I am the Blessed One.

concepts.title: Involution Precedes Evolution
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda was talking to people in 1896, when Darwin was the new exciting thing and "evolution" was on everyone's lips.

concepts.title: The Microcosm: The Self-Luminous Soul
concepts.excerpt: The moon shines — but not with its own light. It's borrowing the sun's.

concepts.title: Immortality: The Soul as Non-Compound
concepts.excerpt: Here's Vivekananda's whole argument for immortality in one move: only things that were built can fall apart.

concepts.title: The Three Vedānta Schools: Dualism to Advaita
concepts.excerpt: Indian philosophy, Vivekananda says, gave three big answers to the question "what is the relationship between God, the soul, and the world?"

concepts.title: Saṃskāra, Reincarnation, and Self-Made Destiny
concepts.excerpt: Picture a ball in a room, and everyone has a mallet. People hit it from all sides — hundreds of blows, driving it from corner to corner.

concepts.title: The Real and the Apparent Man: The Three Destinies and the Living-Free
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda once walked for weeks across a desert on the Indian coast.

concepts.title: Unity in Diversity: Heavens Are States, Not Places
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda kept thinking that if he just got to the right place, he'd see clearly.

concepts.title: Anti-Fanaticism: Fanatics Cannot Work
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda has a blunt, almost mechanical objection to fanaticism: it's inefficient.

concepts.title: Buddha and Shankara: Heart and Intellect Combined
concepts.excerpt: Vivekananda holds up two of India's greatest figures and says: each one had half of what the religion of the future needs.

concepts.title: Samuel's Critical-Anthropological Method
concepts.excerpt: Picture a scholar in his Oxford college rooms in late 2002, preparing the Wilde Lectures.
